The Sin-Zing-Zuh (新识诚 'New Knowledge'), Volume 6, published the following article written by one Wei Zung (怀成) :-

WHY SO MANY INCIDENTS?

During recent years, China has been faced with many domestic and external troubles, especially after the Mukden Incident of September 18, 1931, all of which have given rise to "gross misunderstandings" and "unfortunate incidents".

So far as we can recollect many misunderstandings and incidents have taken place since the January 28th Incident in Shanghai. Take, for instance, the murder of the Japanese marine named Hideo Nakayama which took place sometime in June (? November) last year in the Hongkew district. It was alleged that this murder was a preliminary step in the anti-Japanese movement of the Chinese people. For this reason, immediately after the incident took place, our "friendly nation" at once definitely asserted that the murder was perpetrated by Chinese. Later, a certain clue was obtained and several Chinese were arrested and they admitted that they were the persons who had murdered the Japanese marine. This ended the Nakayama murder case. Later, similar incidents took place in Pakhoi, Swatow, Chengtu, Hankow and even Taiyuan, Shansi Province.

The attempted murder of a family couple of our "friendly nation" took place not long ago in Hongkew. Fortunately, due to the fact that one of the couple sustained only a slight injury to the ear, the incident did not give rise to any serious misunderstanding.

But it must be noted that such incidents do not take place without cause. Although the circumstances surrounding these incidents differ, yet the principal cause is the same. The forcible occupation of our North-eastern territory by our "friendly nation" has aroused anti-Japanese feeling among the Chinese; if our "friendly nation" did not take advantage of the anti-Japanese movement as a pretext to intimidate and oppress our Government preparatory to further acts of aggression or to demanding certain privileges, there would not have been so many unfortunate incidents.

We do not deny that some of our fellow-countrymen have resorted to foolish and stupid acts in their indignation, but the cause of it all is due to the aggression of our "friendly nation". We do not approve of such acts; we strongly object to assassination of individuals. We advise such people to reserve their energy for activities that are beneficial to the whole country.

In order to overthrow our real enemy - the Imperialists in the Far East - we should first consolidate ourselves. The persons we want to kill are not the subjects or the soldiers of a certain enemy nation, for it is their masters -- the executioners -- who are responsible for the state of our country.

为何事件频发？

近年来，中国面临诸多内忧外患，尤其是自1931年9月18日沈阳事变以来，所有这些都引发了“严重的误解”和“不幸的事件”。

据我们要回忆，自上海一·二八事变以来，已发生许多误解和事件。例如，去年六月（？十一月）左右在虹口地区发生的日本海军陆战队士兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）被杀案。有人声称这起谋杀是中国人民反日运动的初步行动。因此，事件发生后，我们的“友邦”立即断言该谋杀系中国人所为。随后，获得某些线索，几名中国人被捕，并承认他们是杀害该名日本海军陆战队士兵的凶手。中山谋杀案至此结案。后来，类似的案件发生在北海、汕头、成都、汉口，甚至山西省太原。

不久之前，在虹口发生了一起针对我们“友邦”一对夫妇的谋杀未遂案。幸运的是，由于夫妇中一人仅耳朵受轻伤，该事件并未引起任何严重的误解。

但必须指出，此类事件的发生并非无缘无故。尽管这些事件的具体情况各不相同，但主要原因是一样的。我们的“友邦”强行占领我国东北领土，激起了中国人的反日情绪；如果我们的“友邦”不利用反日运动作为借口来恐吓和压迫我国政府，为进一步的侵略行为或索取某些特权做准备，就不会有这么多不幸的事件发生。

我们不否认，一些同胞出于愤慨采取了愚蠢和拙劣的行动，但这一切的根源在于我们“友邦”的侵略。我们不赞成此类行为；我们强烈反对暗杀个人。我们建议这些人将精力保留用于对国家整体有益的活动。

为了推翻我们真正的敌人——远东的帝国主义者——我们首先应该巩固自身。我们要杀的人不是某个敌对国家的臣民或士兵，因为是他们的主人——刽子手——对我们国家的现状负有责任。

Simultaneous with this explanation, we desire
to state that, although we have had absolutely no connection
whatever in any of the unfortunate incidents, yet we have
been held responsible for them. Take, for instance, the
"Japanese murder case". According to the reports published
by the "Hwa Mei Sun Pao", the case is obviously one
involving a love affair among Japanese, yet the Japanese
military authorities at once definitely alleged that it
was the work of Chinese.
Ever since the "New Life Weekly" case which arose
out of the publication of an article entitled "Gossip
about Emperors", our Government has repeatedly promulgated
orders restricting freedom of speech. Countless number
of persons who could not withhold their patriotism have
thus been imprisoned on a charge of harming the diplomatic
relations of the country. But has this reduced the number
of unfortunate incidents? From this, we can see that "to
put on a smiling face after being slapped" and "to offer
concessions according to the wishes of others" can have
no satisfactory results. If the Government were to follow
the wishes of the people and resolutely reject the demands
of the enemy, it will be able to recover the lost territory
and frustrate the dirty tricks of the enemy.

It is being suggested that every Japanese resident should carry a police whistle.

CHINESE SEAMEN AT SAN FRANCISCO FORM ANTI-JAPANESE NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION AT THE INSTIGATION OF AMERICAN PUBLIC BODIES

The Shanghai Seamen's Association has sent a telegram to the Association suggesting co-operation.
This is part of the movement to unite the various National Salvation Associations in China with similar associations abroad for the purpose of furthering anti-Japanese activities in foreign countries.
The expenses of the Seamen's National Salvation Association are paid by several American public bodies and Chinese residents in America. Thus, it would seem that foreign countries are assisting the anti-Japanese movement.

China Times (Nanking Telegram):

THE INSPECTION OF FACTORIES

In connection with the question of the inspection
of factories in the International Settlement, the Ministry
of Industry, after conferring with the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs, has drawn up a set of measures which have been
forwarded to the Executive Yuan for consideration. It is
learned that the Ministry of Industry will soon notify the
Shanghai City Government of these measures so as to enable
the latter to resume the negotiations with the S.M.C.
It is said that these measures will authorize
the S.M.C. to undertake the inspection of factories in the
International Settlement; a Factory Inspectorate composed
of officials nominated by both the Chinese authorities and
the S.M.C. will be established to undertake the inspection
of factories in the Settlement.

Sin Wan Pao (Peiping Telegram):

THE SITUATION IN SUIYUAN

Fighting has not yet broken out in East Suiyuan.
On the morning of November 5, five Japanese aeroplanes
reconnoitered the regions held by the Suiyuan Provincial
troops.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

JAPANESE ATTACKED AND WOUNDED

At 7.35 p.m. yesterday while a Japanese named
Mr. Kagoshima, age 35, residing at No.83 Kashing Road, was
walking together with his wife and his son in front of
House No.10 Pao Tuh Li (宝德里), Jukong Road, a man, wearing
black short clothing, came up from behind and attempted
to stab the Japanese in the head. The Japanese moved his
head to the left with the result that the knife wounded
him in the neck. The assailant escaped through a small
alleyway behind the Moon Palace Hotel. The knife was later
found in the alleyway and was taken to the North Szechuen
Road Police Station. The Chinese Police made an investi-
gation of all residents living in the area of the trouble.
House No.8 which is next to House No.10 is a coffee shop
opened by a Japanese.
Mr. Liang Hu Tso (梁扶初), Officer-in-Charge
of the North Station Branch of the Public Safety Bureau,
accompanied by Assistant Superintendent Wong Vee Min (王惟明),
visited the scene to make an investigation. In the meantime,
Mr. Tajima, Officer-in-Charge of the First Section of the
Japanese Consular Police, together with 14 Japanese marines,
had arrived and conducted an investigation with the assistance
of the Chinese Police.

for treatment. Later he returned to his home.

昨晚7时35分，一名叫鹿儿岛（Kagoshima）的日本男子，现年35岁，居住在嘉善路83号，正与其妻子和儿子在虬江路宝德里10号门前行走时，一名身穿黑色短衣的男子从背后走近，试图刺该日本人的头部。该日本人向左转头，结果刀刺中其颈部。袭击者通过月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）后面的一条小巷逃脱。后来在巷子里发现了这把刀，并被送往北四川路警察局。中国警察对事发区域的所有居民进行了调查。紧邻10号的8号房屋是一家由日本人开设的咖啡店。
公安局北站分局局长梁扶初（Liang Hu Tso）在副督察王惟明（Wong Vee Min）陪同下，前往现场进行调查。与此同时，日本领事馆警察第一课课长田岛（Tajima）先生带领14名日本海军陆战队员抵达，并在中国警察的协助下进行了调查。
鹿儿岛先生向日本海军陆战队司令部报告了此次袭击，但未去医院治疗。随后他返回家中。

November 6, 1936.

NIPPO , MAINICHI AND NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE STABBED BY CHINESE NEAR ISIS THEATRE

At 7.20 p.m. November 5 a
Japanese named Shigeru Kagoshima, age 34, in company
with his wife Kiyono, age 34, a son named Hamoru, age 5, and
a second son named Katashi, age 2, was walking in front of
the "Cafe Heart(?) behind the Isis Theatre on Jukong
Road, Chapei, when a Chinese suddenly approached from
behind and stabbed him in the neck with a dagger inflicting a
superficial flesh wound about three inches long under right
ear. The assailant made good his escape. The victim
immediately reported the incident to a Japanese marine
sentry on duty in front of the Japanese Nishi Honganji
Temple on Range Road and to the Marine post on
Chapoo Road. Mr. Kagoshima is an employee of the
Shanghai Kemban Association of Japanese Restaurants; he
resides at No. 83 Kashing Road.
The Japanese Special Naval Landing
Party and the Bureau of Public Safety immediately dispatched
officers to the Jukong Road District for guard duty and
investigation.
Mr. Kitamura, Chief of the
Japanese Consular Police expressed the hope that Japanese
residents will not take thoughtless action but will
leave the matter in the hands of the authorities.

A dagger discovered

Soon after the stabbing, the
Chapei Police discovered the dagger which was used in
the attack at a spot between No. 9 and No. 8(Cafe Heart)
about 60 feet away from the scene of crime.
Mr. Yukichi Sakagami of the
Restaurant Togo and Mr. Ketaro Maruyama of the Restaurant
Ichimatsu who saw the Chapei Police find the dagger stated
as follows:- "When we saw the dagger being picked up
by the Chapei Police, it looked like a bayonet. The
point was stained with blood. The policeman who picked
up the dagger took the dagger to the North Szechuen
Road Branch Station and claimed that the dagger belonged
to him. It is rather strange to hear that a blood
stained, naked dagger belonged to a uniformed policeman."

The victim's wife made the following statement.

"At a warning shouted by my husband,
I turned my head and saw a Chinese of about 5 feet and 6
inches in height running away. He wore a short coat and
trousers but no hat. The colour of his clothing was not
clear because the place was dark."

Mr. S. Fukai, a friend of Mr. Kagoshima, states
as follows regarding his character:-
"Mr. Kagoshima is a very kind
man who talks very little. He is not a sort of man who
would have enemies."

一名日本人在伊西斯剧院附近被中国人刺伤

11月5日晚7时20分，一名叫鹿儿岛茂（Shigeru Kagoshima）的日本人，现年34岁，与其妻清野（Kiyono，34岁）、长子滨雄（Hamoru，5岁）和次子片士（Katashi，2岁）在闸北虬江路伊西斯剧院（Isis Theatre）背后的“心咖啡馆”（Cafe Heart(?)）前行走时，一名中国人突然从背后接近，用匕首刺其颈部，造成右耳下方约三英寸长的浅表皮肉伤。袭击者成功逃脱。受害者立即向在兰路（Range Road）日本西本愿寺（Nishi Honganji Temple）前执勤的日本海军哨兵以及乍浦路海军岗哨报告了此事。鹿儿岛先生是上海日本餐馆组合（Shanghai Kemban Association of Japanese Restaurants）的雇员；他居住在嘉善路83号。
日本特别海军陆战队和公安局立即派遣人员前往虬江路地区执行警卫任务和进行调查。
日本领事馆警察署长北村（Kitamura）先生表示，希望日本居民不要采取轻率行动，而是将此事宜交由当局处理。

发现一把匕首

刺杀发生后不久，闸北警察在距犯罪现场约60英尺处的9号和8号（心咖啡馆）之间发现了用于袭击的匕首。
东乡餐厅（Restaurant Togo）的坂上雄吉（Yukichi Sakagami）先生和一松餐厅（Restaurant Ichimatsu）的丸山启太郎（Ketaro Maruyama）先生在目睹闸北警察发现匕首后陈述如下：“当我们看到闸北警察捡起匕首时，它看起来像是一把刺刀。刀尖沾有血迹。捡起匕首的警察将匕首带到北四川路分巡捕房，并声称这把匕首属于他。听说一把沾满血迹的无鞘匕首属于一名制服警察，这相当奇怪。”

受害者的妻子作了如下陈述。

“在我丈夫喊出警告时，我转过头，看到一个身高约5英尺6英寸的中国人逃跑。他穿着短外套和裤子，但没有戴帽子。由于地方昏暗，衣服的颜色看不清楚。”

鹿儿岛先生的朋友深井 S.（S. Fukai）先生就其为人陈述如下：
“鹿儿岛先生是一个非常善良的人，很少说话。他不是那种会结仇的人。”

China Times (Nanking Telegram):

THE INSPECTION OF FACTORIES

In connection with the question of the inspection
of factories in the International Settlement, the Ministry
of Industry, after conferring with the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs, has drawn up a set of measures which have been
forwarded to the Executive Yuan for consideration. It is
learned that the Ministry of Industry will soon notify the
Shanghai City Government of these measures so as to enable
the latter to resume the negotiations with the S.M.C.
It is said that these measures will authorize
the S.M.C. to undertake the inspection of factories in the
International Settlement; a Factory Inspectorate composed
of officials nominated by both the Chinese authorities and
the S.M.C. will be established to undertake the inspection
of factories in the Settlement.

Sin Wan Pao (Peiping Telegram):

THE SITUATION IN SUIYUAN

Fighting has not yet broken out in East Suiyuan.
On the morning of November 5, five Japanese aeroplanes
reconnoitered the regions held by the Suiyuan Provincial
troops.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

JAPANESE ATTACKED AND WOUNDED

At 7.35 p.m. yesterday while a Japanese named
Mr. Kagoshima, age 35, residing at No.83 Kashing Road, was
walking together with his wife and his son in front of
House No.10 Pao Tuh Li (宝德里), Jukong Road, a man, wearing
black short clothing, came up from behind and attempted
to stab the Japanese in the head. The Japanese moved his
head to the left with the result that the knife wounded
him in the neck. The assailant escaped through a small
alleyway behind the Moon Palace Hotel. The knife was later
found in the alleyway and was taken to the North Szechuen
Road Police Station. The Chinese Police made an investi-
gation of all residents living in the area of the trouble.
House No.8 which is next to House No.10 is a coffee shop
opened by a Japanese .
Mr. Liang Hu Tso (梁扶初), Officer-in-Charge
of the North Station Branch of the Public Safety Bureau,
accompanied by Assistant Superintendent Wong Vee Min (王惟明),
visited the scene to make an investigation. In the meantime,
Mr. Tajima, Officer-in-Charge of the First Section of the
Japanese Consular Police, together with 14 Japanese marines,
had arrived and conducted an investigation with the assistance
of the Chinese Police.
Mr. Kagoshima reported the attack to the Japanese
Landing Force Headquarters, but did not go to a hospital
for treatment. Later he returned to his home.

My name is Miss Kimi Yamashita, age 29, I am a Japanese
subject. I reside in Room No. 5 of a foreign-boarding-house

At about 9.05 p.m. on the 12/11/36 I left my friend's home

We walked along Park Lane in a southerly direction towards

south intending to go to my home at 453 Boone Road. Just as I
was crossing Quinsan Road the male Chinese whom I had seen
loitering, began to follow me walking behind me within two or
three feet of me. I became afraid of the man and so paused and
glanced round to see my friend walking away just to allow the
man to pass me.

walked on along Quinsan Garden Road towards Boone Road. I
followed him walking about 6 or 7 feet behind him.

known as Quinsan Garden which runs between Quinsan Garden Road

我们沿着派克路向南朝昆山路方向行走。到达派克路与昆山路拐角处时，我们道别后分开。我的朋友沿昆山路向东走去。
就在那时，我注意到一名中国男子在昆山路与派克路的西北角徘徊。我穿过昆山路进入昆山花园路，仍向南走，打算回到昆山路453号的家中。正当我穿过昆山路时，我之前看到的那名徘徊的中国男子开始跟随我，走在我身后两三英尺的地方。我对这个人感到害怕，于是停下来回头看了一眼，看到我的朋友正在走远，只是为了让那个人从我身边经过。

Date ____ / ____ / ____

Ta Kung Pao :-

FRUIT DEBRIS FALLS ON JAPANESE MARINE.

At about 9 p.m. yesterday an alarm was caused on North Szechuen Road when Lee Feng Fah (龐分法), aged 26, native of Ningpo, a coolie of the Shing Lee Bakery (兴利麵包公司), No. 172 Yue Ching Fong Alleyway (餘慶坊) off North Szechuen Road, threw out of a window of his room on the second floor some lung-an shells and other debris which, by chance, fell upon a Japanese marine on post duty near the place.

Regarding the act as an insult, the Japanese marine entered the bakery to inquire into the matter and attempted to take Lee Feng Fah to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.

As a result of a consultation between Inspector Liang Foo Tsoo (梁扶初) of the North Railway Station Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety and an Inspector of a Settlement Police Station, it was agreed that the coolie Lee Feng Fah and a responsible person of the bakery be taken to the North Szechuen Road Police Station of the Bureau of Public Safety for interrogation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

TROUBLE BETWEEN BUS CONDUCTORS AND CHAPEI POLICEMEN.

At about 9 a.m. yesterday, bus No.4902 of the No.4 Route of the Chinese Bus Company, operating between the Civic Centre and Paoshan Road, was boarded by about six policemen. When the conductor named Wong Hai Yung (王海榮) approached them for fares, a fight took place at Hwa Yuan Ka (花園街), as a result of which the conductor was injured in the head. The bus was then driven to the North Railway Station Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety. A request for the punishment of the policemen was of no avail. Subsequently the entire body of drivers and conductors of the No.1 Route buses travelling between Chapei and Kiangwan and No.4 and No.5 Route buses travelling between Paoshan Road and the Civic Centre went on strike.

Upon hearing of the trouble, the Bureau of Public Safety detailed the Deputy Chief of the Superintendent's Office to assist Liang Foo Tsoo, Inspector in charge of the North Railway Station Branch of the Public Safety Bureau, to discuss the trouble with representatives of the Chinese Bus Company and the Sixth District Bus Company Workers Union and to persuade the strikers to resume work. Policeman No.2109 and the other officers concerned were stripped of their uniforms and removed to the Headquarters of the Public Safety Bureau to be dealt with according to law.

The entire body of strikers resumed work at 10.15 a.m.

（印：DEPUTY SUPERINTENDENT 28 SEP. 1936 CRIME BRANCH）

水果残渣落在日本海军陆战队员身上。

昨晚约晚上9时，北四川路发生警报，事件起因是兴利麵包公司（位于北四川路餘慶坊172号）的一名26岁宁波籍苦力李凤法（Lee Feng Fah，音译），从其二楼房间的窗户向外扔出一些龙眼壳及其他杂物，这些杂物碰巧落在了附近执勤的一名日本海军陆战队员身上。

该日本海军陆战队员认为此举是一种侮辱，遂进入麵包店查询此事，并试图将李凤法带往日本海军陆战队总部。

经公安局北站分局督察梁扶初（Liang Foo Tsoo）与一租界警局督察协商后，双方同意将该苦力李凤法及麵包店一名负责人带至公安局北四川路警察局接受讯问。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

巴士售票员与闸北警察之间的纠纷。

昨日上午约9时，中华汽车公司行驶于市中心与宝山路之间的4路公共汽车（车号4902）上上了约六名警察。当名为王海榮（Wong Hai Yung）的售票员向他们收取车费时，在花園街（Hwa Yuan Ka，音译）发生斗殴，导致售票员头部受伤。随后该巴士被开往公安局北站分局。要求惩处警察的请求未获结果。此后，行驶于闸北与江湾之间的1路公共汽车，以及行驶于宝山路与市中心之间的4路和5路公共汽车的所有司机和售票员全体罢工。

公安局获悉此纠纷后，指派 superintendent 办公室副主任协助负责公安局北站分局的督察梁扶初，与中华汽车公司及第六区公共汽车业工会代表商讨此纠纷，并劝说服罢工者复工。第2109号警员及其他有关警官被剥去制服，并移送公安局总部依法处理。

全体罢工者于上午10时15分复工。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, September 26, 1936.

Unhappy Happyland Head
Gets Life Term Commuted

MR. HU YUNG-NIEN, unhappy proprietor of the Happyland Cabaret on North Szechuen Road, is happier today because hopes loom on the horizon that his "life sentence" may soon be commuted.

The cabaret proprietor was "sentenced" to call on the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party every afternoon "as long as he lives" to report on the results of the search for a patron who intentionally or unintentionally threw a pear core that hit the back of the neck of a Japanese bluejacket on Monday night.

Two persons have now been nabbed for the "Pear Core Incident" that caused much stir in Hongkew, only to be overshadowed by the murder of a seaman on Yalu Road Wednesday night. They are now detained by the North Station branch of the Public Safety Bureau for questioning. If they prove to be the right men, Mr. Hu will not have to call on the Japanese headquarters any more.

The arrested persons are Mr. Huang Ling-shaw, instructor at the "Happy Life" Dancing School, and Hsu Zau-ning, a tea-boy in the same institution. They were taken into custody by Chinese police late Thursday night, it was revealed this morning. The Chinese police will prosecute the pair for creating the "Pear Core Incident."

Mr. Hu found his daily trips to the Japanese Headquarters an unpleasant job during the last few days. Going through a bristling ring of shining bayonets and the cordon thrown out by Japanese bluejackets as result of the latest Hongkew incident made Mr. Hu wish that he had ever called himself Yung-nien, which means "Perpetual Life." He is much relieved today, however, now that the alleged culprits have been rounded up.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年9月26日，星期六。

不幸的“快乐世界”老板
无期徒刑获减刑

胡永年先生，北四川路“快乐世界”舞厅的不幸老板，今天心情较好，因为希望浮现，他的“无期徒刑”可能很快获得减刑。

这位舞厅老板被“判处”在其“余生”中每天下午前往日本海军陆战队总部报到，汇报搜寻一名顾客的结果，该顾客在周一晚上有意或无意地扔出一个梨核，击中了一名日本水兵的后颈。

目前已有两人因引发虹口极大轰动的“梨核事件”而被捕，但该事件随即被周三晚上鸭绿江路发生的一起水兵谋杀案所掩盖。他们现被公安局北站分局拘留审讯。如果证实他们确是肇事者，胡先生就无需再前往日本总部报到了。

被捕者是“快乐人生”舞蹈学校的教员黄灵绍（Huang Ling-shaw，音译）和该机构的茶役徐造宁（Hsu Zau-ning，音译）。今晨披露，这两人是在周四深夜由中国警察拘捕的。中国警方将以制造“梨核事件”为由起诉这两人。

胡先生发现过去几天每天前往日本总部的行程是一件令人不快的差事。穿过因最近虹口事件而部署的日本水兵组成的寒光闪闪的刺刀环和警戒线，让胡先生希望自己从未取名叫“永年”，因为这意味着“永久生命”。然而，随着嫌疑犯被 roundup，他今天如释重负。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, September 23, 1936

"In The Neck"

WE READ in a morning contemporary
that excitement ran high Monday night
in the Hongkew district when a member of
the Japanese Naval Patrol was hit in the
back of the neck by a pear core allegedly
thrown out of the window of the Happyland
Cabaret on North Szechuen Road.
No details, unfortunately, seem available
as to the amount of pear still adhering to
the core, and we regard this as a reflection
on the reporter covering the story. If there
were still one or two sizeable bites of pear left
on the core, this would augur a state of ex-
citement and perhaps of active anti-Japanese
feeling on the part of its ex-owner. On the
other hand if the core were well "chewed"
this would indicate that it was all merely a
rub of the green and just one of those re-
grettable incidents likely to happen to anyone
traversing North Szechuen Road in the
vicinity of the Happyland Cabaret.
High tension existed in the vicinity for
some time, after the Naval Patrol had thrown
a cordon around the cabaret, we read. But
with relief we find that this eased off after
an investigation had been launched by
officials.
The owner of the Happyland was of course
hurried off to the North Station Branch of
the Bureau of Public Safety and interrogated,
finally being released with a caution.
"A careful search was made of the
cabaret and of the rooms above it," continues
the news story. "Peelings of pears were found
by Bureau of Public Safety officers in
spittoons in the dance hall and on the
balcony." This adds up nicely, of course, al-
though the fact that at least part of the pear
had been eaten probably prevented the officers
from identifying which specific peelings be-
longed to that pear-core which so outrageous-
ly smote the Naval Patrol man in the back
of the neck.
Japanese photographers and news men
were soon on the scene and it was reported
that six flashlight photos were taken of the
spot where the "incident" occurred; after which
the gentlemen of the press entered the Happy-
land Cabaret (strictly for business purposes)
and took several pictures of the interior and
its occupants, no doubt including the spittoons
and the pear peelings, but probably omitting
the pear core and the back of the victim's
neck in view of the gravity of the whole mat-
ter.
Whatever the outcome of this latest in-
cident it seems certain that on North Sze-
chuen Road way there will be no more re-
sorts to such phrase
"upsetting the equilibrium of a
sober citizen who has imbibed, etc." syn-

“击中颈部”

我们从一份晨报中读到，周一晚上虹口区情绪高涨，当时一名日本海军巡逻队员被一个据称从北四川路“快乐世界”舞厅窗户扔出的梨核击中了后颈。
遗憾的是，关于梨核上还粘附有多少梨肉似乎没有细节可供参考，我们认为这是对报道此事的记者的一种反映。如果梨核上还留有一两口 sizable 的梨肉，这将预示其前主人处于兴奋状态，甚至可能存在积极的反日情绪。另一方面，如果梨核被充分“咀嚼”过，这表明这仅仅是一次意外，只是任何经过“快乐世界”舞厅附近北四川路的人都可能遇到的那种令人遗憾的事件之一。
我们读到，在海军巡逻队对舞厅实施包围后，该地区紧张局势持续了一段时间。但令我们宽慰的是，在官员展开调查后，局势得以缓解。
“快乐世界”的老板当然被匆忙带往公安局北站分局并接受讯问，最终在被警告后获释。
新闻报道继续称：“对舞厅及其上方的房间进行了仔细搜查。公安局官员在舞厅和阳台的痰盂中发现了梨皮。”这当然很好地佐证了事实，尽管至少部分梨已被吃掉这一事实可能使官员无法确定哪特定的梨皮属于那个如此恶劣地击中海军巡逻队员后颈的梨核。
日本摄影师和新闻记者很快赶到现场，据报道拍摄了六张闪光灯照片，记录了“事件”发生的地点；随后，新闻界人士进入“快乐世界”舞厅（严格出于业务目的），拍摄了内部及其 occupants 的几张照片，无疑包括痰盂和梨皮，但鉴于整个事件的严重性，可能省略了梨核和受害者后颈的照片。
无论这最新事件的结果如何，可以肯定的是，在北四川路一带，将不再有人诉诸此类短语
“扰乱了一位已饮酒等的清醒公民的平衡，等等。” syn-

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury Wednesday, September 23, 1936

Happyland Proprietor Promises To Spend
Life Time Calling Daily At Headquarters
Of Japanese Until “Pear Core Case” Ends

THE “Happyland Dance Hall Incident,” better known as the “Pear Core Case,” was brought to a happy conclusion late on Monday night, when Hu Yung-nien, the proprietor of the North Szechuen Road cabaret, submitted a written apology to the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party.

Mr. Hu also gave a pledge to call daily, as long as he lives, at the headquarters of the Landing Party to report on the progress of his search for the culprit, who on Monday evening tossed a pear core out of the window at a passing patrol of blue-jackets.

If Mr. Hu succeeds in apprehending the guilty man, he is to take him immediately to the barracks of the Landing Party under the terms of the pledge made in the letter.

The incident had its inception at 7:15 o’clock on Monday evening, when a pear core flew out of the window of the Happyland and struck a marine on the neck.

The patrol was immediately called to a halt, the Chinese police were notified, Japanese naval officers were summoned, and an inquiry was launched to determine whether the throwing of the pear core was accidental or was a deliberate insult to the Navy.

Merrymaking came to a halt in the Cabaret as the police proceeded to inspect spittoons and search rooms above the dance hall, to determine from where the core had come.

Captain Liang Wu-chu, chief of the North Station branch of the Bureau of Public Safety, who hastened to the spot shortly after the “incident,” was in charge of the investigations.

He it was who took Hu the Owner to the police station for questioning.

Tomorrow afternoon, at 4 o’clock, Hu will make his third call at the headquarters of the Special Naval Landing Party to report that the culprit has not yet been found.

Note: Editorial comment on the “pear core incident” appears on page 10 today.

“快乐世界”老板承诺在有生之年每日前往日本总部报到
直至“梨核案”结束

被称为“梨核案”的“快乐世界舞厅事件”在周一晚上圆满解决，当时北四川路舞厅老板胡永年向日本特别海军陆战队提交了书面道歉。

胡先生还承诺，在其有生之年，每天前往陆战队总部报到，汇报其搜寻肇事者的进展，该肇事者在周一晚上向路过的水兵巡逻队从窗口扔出一个梨核。

如果胡先生成功抓获罪犯，根据信中作出的承诺条款，他将立即将其带往陆战队营房。

该事件始于周一晚上7点15分，当时一个梨核从“快乐世界”的窗户飞出，击中了一名海军陆战队员的颈部。

巡逻队立即停止行进，通知了中国警察，召来了日本海军军官，并展开了调查，以确定扔梨核是意外还是对海军的故意侮辱。

随着警察检查痰盂并搜查舞厅上方的房间以确定梨核来源，舞厅内的娱乐活动停了下来。

公安局北站分局局长梁武初（Liang Wu-chu，音译）在“事件”发生后不久赶赴现场，负责调查工作。
正是他将老板胡带往警察局进行讯问。

明天下午4点，胡将第三次前往特别海军陆战队总部报到，汇报尚未找到肇事者。

注：关于“梨核事件”的社论评论见今日第10版。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao (September 22) :-

THE INCIDENT AT HAPPYLAND DANCE HALL.

On the night of September 21, North Szechuen Road was thrown into a state of commotion owing to a trivial incident. Fortunately, due to the calm attitude of both the Chinese and Japanese authorities, the matter was amicably settled.
The following are the facts in the incident :-

At about 7.40 p.m. September 21, as two Japanese officials of the Landing Party were passing by the Happyland Dance Hall in the vicinity of the Isis Theatre on North Szechuen Road, two pieces of pear peelings fell on one of the officers. The officer ceased walking. He evidently regarded this as a deliberate act and as an indirect insult to the Japanese Imperial Navy. He immediately notified the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters which at once detailed a number of men to guard the vicinity of the dance hall. A search was then made of the cabaret in conjunction with officials of the Settlement Police and the Bureau of Public Safety. For a time, North Szechuen Road was thrown into a state of panic. The patrons of the dance hall and its employees were terrified as they were not allowed to move about. It seemed as if something serious was about to befall them.

As a result of the search, one of the patrons of the dance hall admitted having thrown out several pieces of pear peelings a few minutes ago. The man was taken away by the officers of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. After some interrogation, it was ascertained that he had no intention to throw the peelings at the officer. The man tendered an apology to the Japanese authorities and was released on guarantee furnished by Liang Fu Tsoo (梁扶和), Officer-in-Charge of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety.

San Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

S.M.C. EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH FRAUD.

In April, 1934 Woo Tsoh Yee (吳竹賢), native of Shanghai, age 31, residing at 79 Hsin Ling Tsung (信陵邨), Rue du Marche, French Concession, the owner of a certain piece of land, desired to apply for a title deed from the Bureau of Land, but did not know the procedure. Upon hearing of this, a friend named Liu Kwang Yee (劉坤賢) informed Woo that he (Liu) had a relation named Yao Ziang Zai (姚盛才) who works in the Bureau of Land, and advised Woo to pay $500 as a fee to get a title deed. On April 21, 1934 Woo delivered $500 to Liu, and the latter gave him a receipt in return. Two years have now elapsed, but nothing has been seen of Liu.

In August this year, Woo filed a prosecution against Liu in the Shanghai Second Special District Court, but Liu did not put in an appearance. The Court then issued a warrant for his arrest. On September 19, Woo met Liu on the street and took him to the Second Special District Court.

《华美晚报》（9月22日）：-

大都会舞厅事件。

9月21日晚，北四川路因一起琐碎事件陷入混乱。幸而由于中日当局态度冷静，此事得以和平解决。
以下是事件事实：-

9月21日晚约7时40分，当两名日本陆战队官员经过北四川路伊西斯剧院（Isis Theatre）附近的大都会舞厅时，两片梨皮落在其中一名官员身上。该官员停下脚步。他显然认为这是故意行为，是对日本帝国海军的间接侮辱。他立即通知日本海军陆战队总部，总部随即派遣多名人员守卫舞厅周边地区。随后，会同租界巡捕及公安局官员对该歌舞厅进行了搜查。一时间，北四川路陷入恐慌。舞厅顾客和员工因被禁止走动而惊恐万分，似乎即将发生严重不幸。

经搜查，一名舞厅顾客承认几分钟前曾向外扔出几片梨皮。该男子被日本海军陆战队官员带走。经审讯，查明他并无向该官员投掷梨皮的意图。该男子向日本当局道歉，并由公安局北站分局局长梁扶和（Liang Fu Tsoo）提供担保后获释。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

工部局雇员涉嫌诈骗。

1934年4月，吴竹贤（Woo Tsoh Yee），上海人，31岁，住法租界马浪路（Rue du Marche）信陵邨79号，系某块土地的所有人，欲向地政局申请地契，但不知办理程序。一位名叫刘坤贤（Liu Kwang Yee）的朋友得知此事后，告知吴某，他（刘某）有一位亲戚姚盛才（Yao Ziang Zai）在地政局工作，并建议吴某支付500元费用以获取地契。1934年4月21日，吴某将500元交给刘某，刘某出具收据。两年已过，刘某杳无音信。

今年8月，吴某在上海第二特区地方法院起诉刘某，但刘某未出庭。法院遂签发逮捕令。9月19日，吴某在街上遇见刘某，并将其带至第二特区地方法院。

Copy from file Report of Officer in charge of Dixwell Road Police Station.
Tuesday, 22nd. Sept. 1936.

THROWING OF
FRUIT AT A
JAPANESE
NAVAL PATROL.
At 7.00.p.m. on the 21-9-36, a telephone message was
received from J.N.P.114 to the effect that pieces of fruit
had been thrown at a Japanese Naval Patrol consisting of
six men, whilst they were marching past the Happy Land
dance hall, No.512 North Szechuen Road, the patrol insisting
that the fruit came from the window of the dance hall.
Officer i/c and Detectives proceeded there and found officers
from the J.N.P. Party, and Supt. Liang officer i/c North
Station, P.S.B. in attendance. From enquiries it would appear
that whilst the patrol were proceeding North along North Sze-
chuen Road, South of Jukong Road, and when passing the Happy
Land Dance Hall, several pieces of fruit, pear cores, were
thrown from an upstairs window of the Dance Hall, which struck
one of the patrol on the left shoulder. A verandah in front
of the dance hall about 4 feet wide on the 1st. floor and sur-
rounded by a sign board was littered with paper and pear
peelings, and it is possible the cores were thrown from there
unintentionally striking the patrol as they fell to the road-
way. Mr. Woo, the owner of the cabaret, who resides on the
2nd. floor above the dance hall, was taken to the J.N.L. Party
Headquarters, by Supt. Liang and in the presence of officers
of the J.N.P. was severely cautioned and released. Flash
light photographs of the Dance Hall interior, occupants and
the outside of the Happy Land Cabaret, were taken by Japanese
reporters and press agents.
D. R. Miss. 63/36.

SUSPECTED
LARCENY IN
CHAPEL INVOL-
VING AN
INDIAN.
At 1.40.p.m. 21-9-36, a telephone message was received
from the North Station, P.S.B. Chapel, to the effect that
they had a British Indian in custody involved in a larceny
charge. Enquiries show that at about 12 noon, 21-9-36
2 Indians, Vir Singh and Lahoru Singh brought to the North
Station, P.S.B. another Indian named Buta Singh, whom they
accused of having stolen a large sum of money and clothing
from their room situated 96 Paoshing Road, the accused also
resides at this address and during the absence of the 2
complainants who have been absent from Shanghai for about 2
months, visiting Weihaiwei pursuing their occupation of
fortune tellers, they returned to Shanghai on the 20-9-36.
At 7.p.m. 20-9-36 Vir Singh gave accused Buta Singh, $1.00
to buy wine which the 3 of them drank together and retired
at about 8.p.m., it was then the accused when being given
the dollar noticed the amount of money in possession of
Vir Singh. On arising at 6.a.m. 21-9-36, Buta Singh had
already gone out and on examining their luggage found that
the money and other property to the value of about $600.00
was missing. On Buta Singh's return **〔此处转录不清〕**
12 noon, they accused him of the theft which he denied.
Full enquiries made by D. Rd. Station detectives when it was
found there was insufficient evidence to support a charge.
D.R.C. **〔此处转录不清〕** present at Station and the case referred
back to the 5th. Div. P.S.B. when Buta Singh was released.

向日本

1936年9月21日晚7时，接到J.N.P.114电话称，当一支由六人组成的日本海军巡逻队行经北四川路512号大都会舞厅时，有人向他们投掷水果碎片，巡逻队坚称水果来自舞厅窗户。
主管警官及侦探前往现场，发现日本海军陆战队（J.N.P.）官员及公安局北站分局主管梁督察（Supt. 印度人的

November 27, 1936. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

ANTI-JAPANESE ELEMENTS ACTIVE SULPHURIC ACID THROWN AT
JAPANESE: INFLAMMATORY HANDBILLS DISTRIBUTED

At about 3.45 p.m. November 25,
while Mr. Hayashi of the Komei Yoko, No. 33 Miller Road,
was reading a magazine at his shop, a Chinese threw a
bottle of sulphuric acid at him. The bottle struck Mr.
Hayashi in the shoulder. Upon rushing out of the shop,
Mr. Hayashi saw a Chinese running away, at the same time
throwing away some handbills. Mr. Hayashi chased the
Chinese to the vicinity of the Higashi Honganji Temple
on Chapoo Road where he lost sight of the man. The
Japanese Consular Police in co-operation with the S.M.P.
later made an investigation to locate the Chinese.
The handbill contained the follow-
ing slogans:-"Slaughter all cold-blooded traitorous merchants",
"Boycotting enemy goods is fundamental way of saving the
nation", "Drive away the Japanese invaders and recover our
lost territory".

JAPANESE RESIDENTS CORPORATION AND THE WATER RATE

Upon learning that the Shanghai
Waterworks Co is about to increase the water rate by 10%,
the Foreign Affairs Negotiations Committee of the Japanese
Residents Corporation held a meeting at noon yesterday
to consider the matter.
The meeting decided to lodge
a protest with the S.M.C. against the increase on the
ground that such an increase was unreasonable at this
time of trade depression.

SEVERE SUPPRESSION OF STRIKERS DESIRED

The strikes of cotton mill
workers started first in the Eastern District and later
spread to the Western District. The strike situation
became quiet after the arrest of several leading members
of the Various Circles National Salvation Association who
were secretly directing the strikes. It is reported that
one or two mills of the Naigai Cotton are still expecting
trouble while the mills of the Nikka Cotton Co. on Ferry
Road are still on strike and the mills in Pootung are
affected.
As the strike has not yet been
settled, it is to be hoped that the authorities concerned
will adopt strict measures to cope with the situation.

TROUBLE AT TSINGTAO

At 5 p.m. November 25 the workers
of the Nippon Cotton Mill in Tsingtao were locked out. The
workers held a demonstration on the street and attacked a
motor car occupied by a son of Mr. Iida, manager of the
Toyoda Cotton Mill, with stones and empty bottles, inflicting
injuries upon the occupants.

1936年11月27日。晨间译文。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

反日分子活跃 硫酸被投向日本人：散发煽动性传单

11月25日下午约3时45分，米勒路（Miller Road）33号光明洋行（Komei Yoko，音译）的林先生（Mr. Hayashi）正在店内阅读杂志时，一名中国人向他投掷了一瓶硫酸。瓶子击中了林先生的肩膀。林先生冲出店外，看见一名中国人逃跑，同时丢弃了一些传单。林先生追赶该中国人至乍浦路（Chapoo Road）东本愿寺（Higashi Honganji Temple）附近，随后失去了目标。日本领事警察与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）合作，随后展开调查以 locating 该中国人。
传单包含以下标语：“屠杀所有冷血的奸商”，“抵制敌货是救国的根本途径”，“驱逐日本侵略者，收复失地”。

日本居留民团与水费

获悉上海自来水公司即将提高水费10%后，日本居留民团外交交涉委员会于昨日中午召开会议审议此事。
会议决定以贸易萧条时期此举不合理为由，向工部局（S.M.C.）提出抗议，反对此次加价。

希望严厉镇压罢工者

棉纺厂工人的罢工始于东区，随后蔓延至西区。在逮捕了几名秘密指挥罢工的各界救国会主要成员后，罢工局势趋于平静。据报道，内外棉纱厂（Naigai Cotton）的一两家工厂仍预计会出现麻烦，而位于斐伦路（Ferry Road，即今丹东路一带）的日华纱厂（Nikka Cotton Co.）的工厂仍在罢工，浦东的工厂也受到影响。
由于罢工尚未解决，希望有关当局采取严厉措施应对局势。

青岛发生骚乱

11月25日下午5时，青岛日本棉纺厂的工人被拒之厂外。工人在街上举行示威，并用石块和空瓶袭击了一辆由丰田纱厂经理饭田先生（Mr. Iida）的儿子乘坐的汽车，致使车内人员受伤。
